north_star: Any agent can turn an unfamiliar phone number into a country-aware, source-backed, uncertainty-honest answer in one lookup.
wedge: A read-only international lookup contract exposed identically through CLI, MCP, HTTP, and the web, beginning with official numbering evidence for NL, GB, and US.
target_user: AI agents and developers building safe unknown-caller experiences.
core_promise: Normalize once, check country-aware evidence, and explain exactly what is known, unknown, and source-supported.
product_principles: Displayed number is evidence context, never proof of caller identity.
Lookups measure demand; only explicit reports affect community evidence.
Every conclusion carries provenance, freshness, and confidence.
Machine-readable contracts lead; human interfaces render the same truth.
non_goals: Expose private subscriber identities or contact-book data.
Claim that a valid number is assigned, reachable, safe, or owned by a named person.
Scrape or republish third-party data without permission or provenance.
Build product features during repository foundation work.
assumptions: Authoritative numbering-allocation data is legally reusable for at least the Netherlands, United Kingdom, and United States.
An explicit origin region is available whenever an input lacks an international country code.
Agents and developers value provenance and calibrated uncertainty over an unsupported identity guess.
A read-only lookup wedge can prove cross-surface parity before community reporting is introduced.
Phone-number portability and spoofing prevent allocation data from proving current provider, subscriber, or caller identity.
success_metrics: A fresh clone validates all repository and .go contracts with one documented command.
CLI, MCP, HTTP, and web adapters can share one versioned lookup output schema.
Every published assessment can be traced to timestamped source evidence and explicit reason codes.
Country coverage can grow through independently testable adapters without weakening safety boundaries.
